title: Empire of Thessalonica
capsule: The Empire of Thessalonica was a short-lived Byzantine successor state established in 1224 when Theodore Komnenos Doukas of the Despotate of Epirus drove out the Latin occupiers and was crowned emperor, directly challenging both Latin Constantinople and the Empire of Nicaea for the Byzantine inheritance. At its height his realm controlled much of Thrace and Macedonia, briefly making it the most powerful Greek state after Latin rule had collapsed. Theodore's ambitions collapsed at the Battle of Klokotnitsa in 1230, where Bulgarian Tsar Ivan Asen II captured and blinded him; his successors Manuel, John, and Demetrios Komnenos Doukas progressively lost ground, and Nicaean emperor John III Doukas Vatatzes annexed Thessalonica outright in 1246.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political history is attested in Byzantine chronicles, but territorial extent fluctuated rapidly between 1224 and 1246 and is reconstructed from narrative sources rather than contemporary cartographic evidence.
